verdicts.factCheck: The llvm-commits archive page for 0212d77 (fetched) states that lowerShiftLeftParts and lowerShiftRightParts used (and Shamt, VT.bits) as the ISD::SELECT condition, that MIPS uses ZeroOrOneBooleanContent so a fold such as select(c, 0, 1) into xor c, 1 miscompiles, that the value is 64 for i128 on MIPS64, and that it fixes issue 235261; it is dated 2026-11-14. The issue page itself returned HTTP 403 to curl, so the issue text was read only through the commit log. MipsISelLowering.cpp at llvmorg-22.1.8 (lines 2684-2688), llvmorg-23.1.0 and release/23.x (lines 2712-2715) still build Cond as a bare ISD::AND; main no longer has that line. kona-client/v1.9.0 mise.toml pins nightly-2026-08-22, which predates the fix, and the cannon target spec is mips64, big endian, +soft-float,+mips64. ruint 1.20.0 bits.rs wrapping_shl on the u256 path computes lo.unbounded_shl and hi.unbounded_shl on u128 halves, so EVM shifts go through the i128 shift-parts lowering. On Ethereum (publicnode, block about 26,487,194) DisputeGameFactory 0xe5965ab5 gameImpls(9) returns 0x19af533c and gameArgs(9) begins with prestate 0x03e5a54835d39c1d83b198314473e1f111c3539c04f65c3e8a9b8ccebe3737c9, so the scanned prestate is the one in use for OP Mainnet type 9. I reran scan_prestate.py on the work directory's text.bin (sha256 of the .bin.gz begins bf144319, as stated): 66 andi rX,rY,0x40 sites, 124 MOVN/MOVZ condition uses, 10 branch zero tests, one srl by 6 (0x10982 at 0x629c4, rd=rt=1, sa=6), and one extra entry the finding did not list: a SPECIAL2 fn 0x24 word 0x70ce7024 at 0x3de7d0, which decodes to dclz r14, r6; it writes r14 and does not read it, so it is a false positive of the scanner and not an arithmetic use. No xori, ori, addu or store reads the masked value. The run log shows 0 mismatches on 85,544 targeted and 96,876 battery vectors and 624, 895 and 1,797 targeted mismatches for the three planted faults.
verdicts.codeCheck: src/libraries/BitMath.sol:16-22 shifts x right by the running r, which reaches 64 to 192 for wide inputs; src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:38 uses sar and signextend and :73 uses shl(and(tick, 0xff), 1); src/libraries/TickMath.sol:142-151 shifts by 127, 128 and f. A wrong SHL or SHR word would change the bitmap slot, tick or price that a swap writes in the proof program, so the dependence the finding describes is real. Nothing in src/ guards against an interpreter that computes a shift wrongly, and nothing needs to on the node itself.
verdicts.corrections: The scanner follows straight-line code for at most 47 instructions and does not follow branch or jump targets, so the prestate check covers uses on the fall-through path only; a use reached through a taken branch would be missed. The use list in the finding omits one scanner entry (dclz at text offset 0x3de7d0), which is a false positive. The value 65 in place of 0 is an extrapolation to MIPS64 of the MIPS32 example in the commit log (0x2100000001 instead of 1). The actor governance is right: adopting a new absolute prestate is a governance act, and with the present prestate there is nothing to exploit.

sources.supports: Commit 0212d77 of 2026-11-14 describes the select condition fault in lowerShift*Parts and fixes issue 235261.
Lines 2684-2688 use the bare AND as the select condition; same in llvmorg-23.1.0 and release/23.x at 2712-2715, absent on main.
eth_call on DGF 0xe5965ab5962edc7477c8520243a95517cd252fa9: gameImpls(9) = 0x19af533c..., gameArgs(9) begins with prestate 0x03e5a548...37c9.

verdicts.factCheck: eth_call on Ethereum (publicnode, latest): DisputeGameFactory 0x43edb88c gameImpls(621) = 0xc08b8ffaf04abb1d7013b74a0e57eccbd7fa5a70; AnchorStateRegistry 0x909f6cf4 respectedGameType() = 0x26d = 621; on 0xc08b8ffa PROOF_THRESHOLD() = 1, version() = 0.3.0, ZK_RANGE_HASH() = 0x3d3713d3...5fdb, TEE_IMAGE_HASH() = 0x73181275...5cbd, all as stated. The Base proof-contracts specification (fetched, HTTP 200) says challengers call challenge() or nullify() with proof material for an intermediate root (line 110), that verifier nullification is a global stop after which verification through that verifier reverts (lines 440-441), and names an allowlist only for TEE proposers in TEEProverRegistry (lines 510, 521); I found no allowlist for ZK challenges. The range program Cargo.lock at base/base 6efa7566 pins revm 42.0.1, revm-interpreter 42.0.0, ruint 1.18.0, alloy-primitives 1.6.1 (which depends on sha3, resolved to 0.11.0 with keccak 0.2.0), and lists the sp1-patches sha3 0.10.8 as patch.unused. The L2BEAT mapping of program hashes to commit 6efa7566 was not refetched by me.
verdicts.codeCheck: src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24-48 depends on MUL, MULMOD, SUB, LT and DIV; src/libraries/BitMath.sol:16-22 on SHR, LT, SHL, OR and BYTE; src/PoolManager.sol:291-297 (take) on the int128 cast and the transfer. A divergent result in the proof build would change pool state roots, which is the dependence the finding states. No divergence was found, so no code path leads to loss.
verdicts.corrections: The test ran a rustc 1.97 rebuild of the crates on an RV64IM emulator, not the published SP1 ELF under Succinct's toolchain and circuits; the finding says so in its preconditions. The actor unprivileged describes who could use a divergence if one existed; with none found the record is info.

clearedSpotChecks.check: For each of the 21 networks: could an opcode the PoolManager runs give another result in the build that settles state than on the node, and could an ordinary account use it.
clearedSpotChecks.note: The parts I could test hold: OP Mainnet type 9 uses prestate 0x03e5a548 (gameArgs(9) read), Base type 621 has threshold 1 and permissionless ZK challenges, Celo and X Layer allowlist challengers. The clearing is qualified for Celo and X Layer (program arithmetic unidentified) and for Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain (private go-ethereum in rc.9), and the kona clearing rests on a linear scan of the prestate that does not follow branch targets. 'No' is accurate only as 'none found'.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Lead L-683 for Celo and X Layer: respected game type, implementation, program and who may prove or challenge.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I queried isAllowedChallenger(0x..beef) and isAllowedProposer(0x..beef) on access managers 0x2c4e8f33 (Celo) and 0xb0998d01 (X Layer): all return false. Celo FALLBACK_TIMEOUT 0x127500 = 1,209,600 s and X Layer 0x757b12c00 = 31,536,000,000 s are in the unit's access.json. An ordinary account cannot challenge; on Celo it could propose after 14 days of proposer silence, which still meets an allowlisted challenger.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Lead L-682: which routines ruint 1.20.0 uses on the kona mips64 target for 64 by 64 to 128 bit products and 128 by 64 divisions, and whether the opcode vectors pass through them.
clearedSpotChecks.note: run_vectors.log shows 0 mismatches on 85,544 targeted and 96,876 battery vectors and nonzero mismatches for each planted fault, so the harness is sensitive. The rebuild uses opt-level 3 rlibs, while the kona justfile builds the release-client-lto profile with a gcc cross linker, so codegen of the real ELF can differ; the prestate scan covers that gap only for the 235261 shape.

leads.question: Extend scan_prestate.py on the respected kona prestate 0x03e5a548 to follow branch and jump targets (or use a disassembler with a control flow graph) from each andi rX,rY,0x40 site, and confirm that no path reads the 0/64 value in xori, ori, addu, daddu, sltu or a store.
leads.why: The current scan follows only straight-line code for 47 instructions; the claim that the respected prestate lacks the LLVM 235261 shape depends on it, and these games are permissionless.
